title: Crypto misuse: HMAC accepts key shorter than FIPS minimum
description: src/providers/wolfssl/wolfssl_hmac.c:116-120 — hmac_sess_init rejects keylen==0 but accepts any keylen from 1 to WOLFSSL_HMAC_MAX_KEY_LEN (128). SP 800-107 Rev 1 §5.3.4 and SP 800-131A Rev 2 Table 3 require HMAC keys to be at least as long as the hash output (32 bytes for HMAC-SHA256, 48 for HMAC-SHA384, 64 for HMAC-SHA512) to achieve the claimed security strength. wolfCrypt does not enforce this. Trigger: caller supplies e.g. keylen=1 to hmac(sha256). Consequence: HMAC is computed with a trivially weak key, producing output with less than the claimed 128-bit security strength. FIPS 140-3 module boundary violation: the module accepts inputs that violate approved mode constraints without returning an error.
